To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the burden experienced by informal caregivers for patients with advanced cancer, dementia, and acquired brain injury is comparable.

the most important predictors of caregiver strain were the number of hours of caregiving per week, the number of hours the caregiver spent on caregiving tasks, and the presence of a comorbid health condition.

1) the burden experienced by family caregivers is not the same for different diseases, 2) the burden is not only related to the disease, but also to the caregiver's own characteristics, 3) the burden is related to the caregiver's perception of the disease, 4) the burden is higher when the patient has a more severe disease, 5) the burden is associated with a higher risk for caregiver depression and anxiety

the burden on informal caregivers is not the same across different diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the caregiver burden of dementia is the greatest of the three conditions and the caregiver burden of brain injury is the least.
informal caregiving in dementia is more burdensome than caregiving in cancer and brain injury, and that the differences are due to the nature of the illness and its trajectory.
